source.title: Quantifying the Effect of Test Set Contamination on Generative Evaluations
source.authors: Rylan Schaeffer; Joshua Kazdan; Baber Abbasi; Ken Liu; Brando Miranda; Ahmed Ahmed; Fazl Berez; Abhay Puri; Stella Biderman; Niloofar Mireshghallah; Sanmi Koyejo

record.tranche_reason: The study fits held-out MATH gold-reference cross-entropy against pretraining compute using a power-law-plus-irreducible-error form, on its own model-size and contamination sweeps. This is the same type of scaling-law measurement, applied in a contamination-focused setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports compute-scaling fits and trends in cross-entropy and Math Verify, which bear on V1, V6, and part of V7. It does not report observed predictions on runs orders of magnitude larger, a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or power-law fits for the later training regimes. Other findings about SFT, overtraining, sampling temperature, solution length, and sequence-position NLL are not rows for the claim versions unless they directly bear on downstream predictability; the sequence-position exceptions concern a different scaling relation.
record.test_reason: For the uncontaminated (R = 0) series, the study fits MATH gold-reference cross-entropy against compute (6ND, 34M–344M params, about 1.4e17–1.4e19 FLOP) with a power law plus irreducible error, and reports a good fit. That is a V1-type result in a new setting: held-out loss on a math benchmark rather than general text. For R > 0 the test set is in the training data, so those series no longer measure held-out loss and do not bear on the claim's versions.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right but incomplete. The authors conclude that contamination raises MATH performance with size and dose through verbatim memorisation, not generalisation. Under scaling-law extrapolation, one replica beats the uncontaminated irreducible error. Overtraining on fresh data dilutes contamination, SFT helps at low and hurts at high contamination, and temperature and solution length expose brittle memorisation in three regimes. They also fix a Math Verify bug in the LM Eval Harness.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a compute-versus-cross-entropy scaling-law fit, but applies it to MATH gold-reference loss in a controlled test-set-contamination experiment with Qwen 3 models up to 344M parameters; model size and token count scale together at 20 tokens per parameter.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted irreducible error, compute prefactor, and compute exponent vary with the number of MATH test-set replicas. The loss–Math Verify association weakens as sampling temperature rises.

fits_no_version.finding: Contaminating pretraining with R replicas of the MATH test set lowers the fitted E from 3.594 to 0.0347 at R = 316 and raises C0 and α. Even one replica puts almost all models below the uncontaminated E.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-set contamination changes the fitted compute-scaling law of benchmark loss and can break the clean-data irreducible-loss floor.

fits_no_version.finding: Math Verify correlates strongly with MATH test loss when the loss varies through contamination. The correlation vanishes above temperature 1.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The loss-to-accuracy link under memorisation depends on sampling temperature.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-token NLL follows a power law plus constant in token index for most size × replica pairs. Exceptions are 34M at R = 0 and 344M at R = 3162 (App. D, Fig. 7, 9, 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context (sequence-position) scaling laws hold for memorised and unmemorised solutions, with stated exceptions.

record.problems: The experiments use a single benchmark, one web-crawl mixture, dense Qwen 3 models only up to 344M parameters, and one model per size/replica tuple. The paper itself says these choices limit extrapolation to frontier scales and other tasks. Scaling-law extrapolation is conditional on assumptions; no observed runs orders of magnitude larger are compared with the fits. Numerical fit coefficients beyond the stated irreducible errors are not transcribed in the text, and uncertainty estimates for the scaling results are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional per-replica fitted coefficient values are given numerically in the text; the remaining coefficients appear in Figure 2. Later-training and sequence-position findings were not extracted as scaling-law results because the study does not fit the claim's pretraining loss-versus-size/data/compute law for those settings.

untested.parts: Separate N-only and D-only laws (N and D co-vary at 20 tokens/param); range beyond about two orders of magnitude of compute; general text loss.
No fitted law is checked against much larger observed runs.
No fixed-compute sweep over the N/D split.
Depth and width follow a single Qwen 3 recipe (Table 2); shape is not varied at fixed N.
No power-law fits for overtraining, SFT, other modalities or repeated-data regimes. Contaminated series are not a clean repeated-data held-out test.
Uncontaminated downstream accuracy stays at floor across 34M–344M, so predictability with scale or loss cannot be assessed.
No comparison of parameter counting, schedules, fitting methods or published splits.

missing.what: Uncontaminated test loss falls as fresh tokens increase at fixed N (overtrain multiplier 1–16, 34M–93M). This bears on the token axis of V1; no fit is given.
Uncontaminated models score near 0% (0.04%) on MATH and its variants at all sizes, a floor for downstream accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Only the R = 0 series is a held-out scaling test; contaminated series measure loss on training data. There is one model per size/replica cell and no uncertainty is reported. Fitted α and C0 values are shown only in Figure 2.

versions.untested_parts: The study fits test-set cross-entropy against compute, with model size and token count increasing together at 20 tokens per parameter. It does not independently vary parameters, tokens, and compute to establish each separate scaling relation or test the non-bottleneck conditions.
It estimates scaling curves and discusses infinite-compute implications, but does not compare predictions fitted on small runs against observed runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute sweep over parameter/token allocations or fitted compute-optimal allocation exponents is reported.
The study does not compare architectures or depth/width alternatives at fixed parameter count.
Although it studies overtraining on fresh data and SFT, it does not test whether the same power-law form holds during those regimes, or in other modalities, repeated-data settings, or transfer.
The reported downstream measure is Math Verify on MATH; other downstream tasks and other evaluation settings are not tested.

Contamination level is varied and fitted scaling coefficients are reported to change. The study does not vary parameter-counting conventions, fitting methods, or schedules to compare their effects, and does not test disagreement between published compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: Qwen 3 architecture causal language models (scaling series)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained from random initialization; 20 tokens per parameter
rows.operation_detail: Fit test-set gold-reference cross-entropy against pretraining compute for each contamination series using L(C,R) = E(R) + C0(R) · C^−α(R), with C ≈ 6ND.
rows.measure: Average fitting error of the compute scaling-law form across contamination series
rows.value: Average fitting error < 10−2 for all R
rows.note: Each contamination series is fit separately; one model was trained per parameter-count and replica-count tuple.
rows.check: Fit error < 1e-2 is stated for all R together. Only the R = 0 series is held-out loss, so only that series bears on V1. N and D co-vary at 20 tokens/param, and compute spans only about two orders of magnitude.

rows.subject: Qwen 3 architecture causal language models (R = 0 scaling series)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained from random initialization; 20 tokens per parameter
rows.operation_detail: Fit test-set gold-reference cross-entropy against pretraining compute for the uncontaminated corpus.
rows.note: The value is an estimate from the fitted scaling law, not an observed loss at a specific compute budget.
rows.check: E = 3.594 is a fitted parameter of the R = 0 law. It supports the power-law-plus-constant form, not V7. Drop the V7 link.

rows.subject: Qwen 3 architecture causal language models (R = 316 scaling series)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained from random initialization; 20 tokens per parameter
rows.operation_detail: Fit test-set gold-reference cross-entropy against pretraining compute for the 316-replica corpus.
rows.note: The authors state that higher replica counts also increase the compute prefactor and compute exponent.
rows.check: In the R = 316 series the test set is training data. Its fitted E measures memorisation of training data, not held-out scaling. Belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen 3 architecture causal language models (contaminated scaling series)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained from random initialization; 20 tokens per parameter
rows.operation_detail: Compare observed model losses in contaminated compute series with the fitted irreducible error for the uncontaminated series.
rows.measure: Whether test-set cross-entropy falls below the R = 0 fitted irreducible error
rows.value: Including even a single replica lets almost all trained models achieve lower cross-entropy than the estimated uncontaminated irreducible error.
rows.note: The authors qualify the infinite-compute implication as conditional on standard scaling-law assumptions; this row reports the finite-run comparison they state.
rows.check: The finding that contaminated losses fall below the uncontaminated E is about contamination, not held-out loss scaling. Belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen 3 architecture causal language models
rows.stage_stated: pretrained from random initialization; 20 tokens per parameter
rows.operation_detail: Compare Math Verify and test-set cross-entropy across model sizes and contamination levels.
rows.measure: Cross-entropy of gold references on the MATH test set
rows.baseline: Smaller models and fewer replicas; numeric baseline not stated
rows.value: Cross-entropies fall as contamination and model size increase; the text reports a sharp improvement around 100 replicas.
rows.note: Model size and token count were not varied independently: pretraining used 20 tokens per parameter.
rows.check: The value mixes contamination and size effects. Only the decrease with model size at R = 0 bears on V1, with N and D scaled together.

rows.subject: Qwen 3 architecture causal language models (scaling series)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained from random initialization; 20 tokens per parameter
rows.operation_detail: Compare fitted compute-scaling coefficients across contamination series.

conditions.value: Different MATH test-set replica counts; text explicitly compares R = 0 and R = 316

rows.measure: Dependence of fitted irreducible error, compute prefactor, and compute exponent on contamination
rows.value: Increasing contamination reduces E from 3.594 at R = 0 to 0.0347 at R = 316; larger R also increases the compute prefactor and compute exponent.
rows.note: The coefficient values other than the two stated E values are shown in the figure but not numerically stated in the text.
rows.check: The exponent and prefactor change with the dose of test-set contamination, so the loss is partly training loss. This is not a setup or fitting choice of the kind V7 names. Belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen 3 architecture causal language models
rows.operation_detail: Assess the association between pretraining loss on MATH and Math Verify score.

conditions.value: The figure compares sampling temperatures; exact values are not stated in the text

rows.measure: Correlation between MATH test-set cross-entropy and Math Verify score
rows.value: The text describes the correlation as strong, weaker at high temperatures, and nearly zero above temperature 1.0.
rows.note: The plotted correlation coefficients are not numerically stated in the text.
rows.check: The caption attributes the loss–accuracy variation to repetition of the test set. That is a memorisation link, not downstream improvement with scale or with held-out loss.

rows.subject: Qwen 3 architecture causal language models
rows.stage_stated: pretrained from random initialization; evaluated with greedy decoding
rows.operation_detail: Measure Math Verify scores across model sizes and contamination levels.
rows.baseline: Uncontaminated models and smaller models; numeric baseline not stated
rows.value: Scores rise with contamination and model size, with performance near baseline at 10 or fewer replicas and a jump around 100 replicas.
rows.note: This is downstream benchmark performance; the paper attributes contamination gains primarily to memorization, not generalization.
rows.check: The rise in Math Verify comes from contamination (memorisation). Uncontaminated models sit near baseline at all sizes (about 0.04% in Table 1), a floor that cannot show predictable improvement with scale.

relationships.condition: Uncontaminated (R = 0) Qwen 3 models, 34M–344M params, 20 tokens/param, MATH gold-reference cross-entropy vs compute (about 1.4e17–1.4e19 FLOP)
relationships.reason: A power law plus irreducible error (E = 3.594) fits loss vs compute with average error < 1e-2, and loss falls with size (R1, R2, R5). The range spans only about two orders of magnitude.
relationships.display_finding: An offset compute power law with irreducible error 3.594 fits loss with average error below 1e-2 across about two orders of magnitude.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
